subject: Urgent: Sustained 5xxs + elevated latency — potential rate/burst throttling
messages:
From: Sara Huang <sara@bridgestone.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and latency starting 08:30 PDT

Hi Aditya / Lauren,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx responses and a jump in median token latency around 08:30 PDT today. Our ingestion workers started retrying aggressively which multiplied traffic — the errors started at ~08:32 and peaked for ~40 minutes. Attached is our request sample and a short incident log.

Symptoms: 
- ~18% 5xx rate for POST /v1/generate between 08:30–09:10
- p50 latency up from 120ms -> 820ms
- multiple clients received 429/503 and many retries succeeded only after ~2 minutes

Can you confirm whether this is an internal rate-limit/quota/burst policy action? We need a timeline because this impacted our production scoring pipeline (affects billing window).

Appreciate a quick triage and expected ETA for full recovery.

—Sara
Sara Huang
Director, Platform Reliability
Bridgestone Analytics

Attachments: request-logs-20280718.csv (CSV excerpt)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Sara — thanks for the report and the logs. We're looking into this now. Quick status:
- I’ve asked infra to pull per-customer rate/quota and burst metrics for BRG (your customer id) for the 08:00–10:00 window.
- Can you confirm whether your clients were performing retry-backoff or blind aggressive retries? The pattern will help us determine if caching/prefix behavior interacted with throttles.

I’ll circle back with a short timeline and a proposed immediate mitigation. Apologies for the disruption; we’ll treat this as P1 until resolved.

—Aditya

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: High error rate and latency starting 08:30 PDT

Folks — quick internal note before I reply to Bridgestone. I’ve been in ops and checked the serving runtime and policy engine; preliminary findings: 

Observations (from infra):
- At 08:31:14 PDT we observed a sudden rise in concurrent open requests for BRG across two GPU pools (pool-a, pool-b).
- The quota controller exhausted the allocated burst credits for BRG and immediately applied the safety valve which reduces per-client inflight by 60% (intended behavior).
- The burst-credit accounting shows credits being drained unusually fast — the credit window was 1 minute but our token accounting was aligning to 15s windows due to an older gating rule left enabled in the policy commit from 06/22.
- Result: the policy double-counted short spikes (15s slices) and considered them repeated bursts instead of a single sustained spike, so the safety valve triggered repeatedly during the 40-minute event.

Immediate corrective steps taken (08:50–09:20):
- Rolled back the gating rule that introduced 15s window alignment (patch: burst-policy-diff.patch).
- Increased BRG burst ceiling by 1.5x as temporary headroom to let queued retries drain (applied at 08:53).
- Tuned safety-valve cooldown to 90s (from 30s) so the controller does not thrash between on/off.

Next steps I’m proposing:
- Postmortem with infra + policy to remove the legacy gating rule and add a canary test to prevent deployments that change window alignment without a rollout flag.
- A short-term credit reconciliation for BRG to estimate successful vs throttled tokens and propose a billing adjustment/credit.
- Formal customer-facing incident note + RCA draft for legal/compliance and for Bridgestone.

I’m attaching the policy diff and a sample of the request log you provided. I’ll follow with a concise reply to Sara with the timeline and ask for their incident export for cross-correlation.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: burst-policy-diff.patch

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Huang <sara@bridgestone.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and latency starting 08:30 PDT

Sara — brief timeline and what we changed (TL;DR: misaligned burst-window gating rule + safety-valve thrash):

What happened:
- 08:31 PDT: BRG traffic spike; our quota controller applied burst accounting but a legacy gating rule caused 15s slices to double-count bursts.
- 08:31–09:10 PDT: Safety valve repeatedly limited inflight (60% reduction) causing higher latency and 5xxs as retries queued and timed out.

What we did (patches applied):
- 08:50 PDT: rolled back the 15s alignment gating rule (patch attached).
- 08:53 PDT: temporarily increased BRG burst ceiling by 50% to allow inflight drains.
- 08:55–09:10 PDT: monitored — 5xxs dropped to <1%, latency returned to baseline by ~09:12 PDT.

Next actions (we need your help):
1) Please send your full incident export (I see you attached a CSV excerpt; full JSON or syslog will help) — we included a shared Drive link for larger files.
2) We will run token-level reconciliation across the affected window and propose a billing credit for throttled requests.
3) We’ll provide an RCA and an action plan by EOD tomorrow (Thu 19 Jul).

Apologies again for the interruption — Lauren has taken ownership of the postmortem and I’m available to sync with your SREs if helpful.

—Aditya
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec: Bridgestone impact and credit approval request

Team — thanks for the swift mitigation and the early timeline. Quick executive update and ask so we can close externally: 

Summary: 
- Incident window: 2028-07-18 08:31–09:12 PDT. Root cause: misapplied gating rule that aligned burst accounting to 15s windows, causing repeated safety-valve activation and effective throttling.
- Customer impact: elevated p50 latency, ~18% 5xx at peak, several hundred thousand tokens retried and several thousand requests timed out (see logs).

Ask (requires exec sign-off): 
1) Approve a goodwill credit for Bridgestone equal to estimated throttled tokens during the window (finance estimate ~ $7,200).
2) Approve the postmortem communication and a one-week follow-up call with their SREs (Lauren to lead).

Risk and mitigation: we patched policy, added a canary for policy commits that change window alignment, and scheduled a postmortem with infra on Mon 2028-07-22.

If there are no objections I’ll route the credit approval through finance/legal this afternoon. We should include a short customer note that avoids technical minutiae but explains the actions and offers the credit.

—Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
